title: Nondeterministic phase host
statement: Let $I$ be a type, let each $i \in I$ have a state type $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$, and let $M_i$ be a nondeterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes over alphabet $\Gamma$ and state type $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$. Given an initial state $q_0$ in the dependent sum of these state types and a function that may redirect each phase state to another dependent-sum state, the phase host has state type $\sum_{i\in I}\mathrm{Ph}(i)$ and initial state $q_0$. At a state $(i,q)$, if the redirect function returns a state, the host makes no writes or output, leaves all heads stationary, and moves to that state; otherwise it performs the transition of $M_i$ for the given choice bit, input symbol, and work-head symbols, embedding any successor state in phase $i$.
hypotheses_covered: A state type $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$ for each phase
A family of machines $M_i$ with $k$ work tapes and alphabet $\Gamma$
A redirection function to optional dependent-sum states
